column1: Tab 1 — State Grid: Energy x Mood (16 cells) — FINAL names/icons, from Capacity Matrix prototype

Cell ID = E{1-4}M{1-4}, per the product specification. Energy: 1=Very Low,2=Low,3=Moderate,4=High. Mood: 1=Very Bad,2=Bad,3=Neutral,4=Good. Never use Energy x Mood as a multiplied score — E4M1 and E1M4 both involve a 4 and a 1 but describe functionally opposite states.

column1: Design note: names, icons, and descriptions above are taken directly from the live Capacity Matrix prototype (as of this handover) and should be treated as final product copy, not proposals — unlike the earlier placeholder version of this tab. If the prototype changes, update here first, then everywhere else in this workbook that references a cell by name (see Tab 9).

Architecture recommendation: store this table (name, icon, description, capacity band, default lean) in a backend-managed configuration/database, not hardcoded in client app code. This lets you rename, reword, or A/B test cells without a new app release, and keeps the recommendation logic in Tabs 2-7 fully server-side. Note this does NOT hide the names from users — once rendered on screen, they are visible to anyone using the app. Backend storage protects your recommendation LOGIC from reverse-engineering; it does not make the visible cell names secret. Protect those instead via trademark registration of the naming system and continued product-market fit.
